codename_map.note: Model codenames (confirmed by the project owner, 2026-11-04): ipnext/watermelon-v0 = Muse Wonder; ipnext/avocado-5.17-v1 = Muse Spark; ipnext/avocado-5.17-v2 = Muse Spark (version variant of the same step-down tier, mapped 2026-11-05 when the watchdog's export first recorded it and make_cost_summary errored on the unknown codename). agents.csv's model column carries the recorded codename (agent.agents.model); make_cost_summary.py resolves each codename through this map to the public model it is priced as. Corroboration, one line: this chat's root agent records ipnext/watermelon-v0, and the runtime independently identifies this session's model as Muse Wonder. Pricing note: the internal build number (5.17) does not correspond 1:1 to a public Spark version; the Spark share is priced as Muse Spark 1.3 Standard, the current public Spark card on the same pricing page.

comment: Hand-maintained API list prices used by make_cost_summary.py. USD per 1M tokens (MTok), standard pay-as-you-go rates. Re-check each source_url before regenerating; update rates and fetched dates together. These are list prices for comparison only - the project itself ran on a Muse subscription, not per-token billing. Each provider entry is a like-for-like tier pair (flagship_tier_model / stepdown_tier_model): in the cost summary the watermelon (Muse Wonder) share of the recorded volume is priced at the flagship tier and the avocado (Muse Spark) share at the step-down tier, for every provider. A provider's upper bound prices the whole volume at its flagship tier.

providers.tier_note: Flagship: Muse Wonder 1.0, Standard mode, pay-as-you-go; Contributor mode is not available for Muse Wonder. This is the serving model's own published rate card: the runtime identifies this chat's model as Muse Wonder (codename ipnext/watermelon-v0). Step-down: Muse Spark 1.3, Standard mode, same pricing page - the tier the project's subagents (codename ipnext/avocado-5.17-v1 = Muse Spark) map to.

Flagship: Claude Opus 5.5 - Anthropic's flagship tier for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work (the pricing page's own description). Step-down: Claude Sonnet 5.5, the Sonnet line directly below Opus on the same pricing page ('the best combination of speed and intelligence'): $2 input / $10 output per MTok; its cache-read (hit) rate is 0.05x base input = $0.10 per MTok (the page's prompt-caching section: a cache hit costs 5% of the standard input price on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5). Cache rates in this entry are cache-READ (hit) rates; Anthropic also charges cache writes (1.25x base for 5-minute, 2x for 1-hour), not modelled here. One tier sits above Opus: Claude Fable 5.1 at $10 input / $50 output / $0.25 cache read.

Flagship: GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's flagship model, Standard processing tier. Step-down: GPT-6.1 Sol, the sibling line directly below GPT-6 Astra in the same Standard table on the pricing page: $2 input / $10 output / $0.10 cached input per MTok. Prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input/cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request (per the official model page); that surcharge is NOT modelled in the headline figures. Cache rate is the cached-input rate; OpenAI also charges cache writes (30-minute write 1.25x uncached input on these models), not modelled here.
